hypothesis: PySnooper's file-output path handling writes trace output to the requested path and preserves the decorated function's return value, but the FileWriter.write method opens the path with the platform-default text encoding, so on a non-UTF-8 locale (LC_ALL=C, PYTHONUTF8=0) writing a trace containing a non-ASCII variable repr raises UnicodeEncodeError instead of producing the trace.
trigger: Decorate a function with @pysnooper.snoop(path) where path is a temporary file, the function has a local variable whose repr contains a non-ASCII character (e.g. 'é'), and run under LC_ALL=C with PYTHONUTF8=0 so the default text encoding is ASCII.

oracle.expected_behavior: After running the decorated function, the requested output path exists and contains the trace, including the non-ASCII variable value, and the decorated function returns its correct result.
oracle.target_evidence: pysnooper/tracer.py FileWriter.write uses open(self.path, 'w' if self.overwrite else 'a') with no encoding argument; get_write_function routes path outputs to FileWriter; tests/test_pysnooper.py test_file_output and test_no_overwrite_by_default assert trace content at the requested path; README documents @pysnooper.snoop('/my/log/file.log').
oracle.historical_evidence: PySnooper:3 historical unit shows the file-output path branch is a real bug surface (path/output variable mismatch), and cookiecutter:1 shows locale-dependent implicit text encoding is a real failure mechanism; combined they suggest probing path-output encoding behavior.

preconditions: Python 3.9.18 with LC_ALL=C, PYTHONUTF8=0, PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0 so locale.getpreferredencoding(False) is ANSI_X3.4-1968/ASCII
pysnooper importable from the buggy checkout

initial_state.named_state: No output file exists at the target path; sys.getdefaultencoding() is utf-8 but locale default text encoding is ASCII

actions.description: Set env LC_ALL=C, PYTHONUTF8=0, PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0 for the test process
Create a temp file path /tmp/pysnooper_plan1/out.log (directory created, file absent)
Define a module-level function decorated with @pysnooper.snoop('/tmp/pysnooper_plan1/out.log') whose body assigns local variable s = 'caf\u00e9' and returns len(s)
Call the decorated function once and capture its return value
Read the bytes of /tmp/pysnooper_plan1/out.log and decode as UTF-8; also record the captured return value

plans.expected_invariant: The decorated function returns 4 and the requested path exists containing a trace line with the non-ASCII repr 'caf\u00e9'

observable.measurement_point: After the decorated function call completes, before any cleanup
observable.extraction_method: open(path,'rb').read().decode('utf-8') and inspect the returned value from the call

assertion.predicate: return_value == 4 AND path exists AND 'caf\u00e9' appears in the decoded trace text
assertion.failure_condition: UnicodeEncodeError raised during the call, or path missing, or trace text lacks the non-ASCII value
assertion.rationale: Directly exercises the path-output branch with a non-ASCII local repr under an ASCII default encoding, so a missing non-ASCII trace or an encode error falsifies the invariant

preconditions: A pre-existing file at the target path containing ASCII text 'lala'

initial_state.named_state: Target path /tmp/pysnooper_plan2/foo.log already exists with content 'lala' and no trailing newline

actions.description: Define a function decorated with @pysnooper.snoop('/tmp/pysnooper_plan2/foo.log') (overwrite default False) whose body sets local variable name = 'na\u00efve' and returns name
Call the decorated function once and capture its return value
Read /tmp/pysnooper_plan2/foo.log as UTF-8 and check it starts with 'lala' and contains 'na\u00efve'

plans.expected_invariant: The decorated function returns 'na\u00efve' and the append-mode file starts with the pre-existing 'lala' followed by a trace containing the non-ASCII repr

assertion.predicate: return_value == 'na\u00efve' AND file content startswith 'lala' AND 'na\u00efve' in file content
assertion.failure_condition: UnicodeEncodeError during append, or pre-existing content lost, or non-ASCII trace absent
assertion.rationale: Exercises the append-mode open path with a non-ASCII repr under ASCII default encoding, distinguishing append behavior from overwrite while measuring the same encoding invariant

preconditions: A pathlib.Path object is accepted as the output argument

initial_state.named_state: No file at /tmp/pysnooper_plan3/out.log; output argument is a pathlib.Path instance rather than str

actions.description: Define a function decorated with @pysnooper.snoop(Path('/tmp/pysnooper_plan3/out.log')) whose body sets local variable greeting = 'h\u00e9llo' and returns greeting.upper()
Call the decorated function once and capture its return value
Read /tmp/pysnooper_plan3/out.log as UTF-8 and check for 'h\u00e9llo' and the return value

plans.expected_invariant: The decorated function returns 'H\u00c9LLO' and the Path-typed output path contains the trace including the non-ASCII repr

observable.source: pysnooper.tracer.get_write_function path branch with pycompat.PathLike input routed to FileWriter

assertion.predicate: return_value == 'H\u00c9LLO' AND file exists AND 'h\u00e9llo' in decoded content
assertion.failure_condition: UnicodeEncodeError, missing file, or non-ASCII trace absent when using a PathLike output
assertion.rationale: Varies the public interface path (PathLike vs str) while still reaching FileWriter.write, so it tests the same encoding invariant through a different supported input boundary
